title: Heidenhain DIN/ISO post: native peck cycles rapid back to the last depth (G205 Q258=0, G200 Q200=0), and PECK posts full retracts

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What happens: the Heidenhain DIN/ISO post writes native peck cycles that do not do the motion of the checked chain. The post writes a native peck only when the R clearance is 0, so Q200 is always 0.
- PECK posts `G205` with `Q258=+0 Q259=+0` and `Q257` equal to `Q202`. The chip-break depth is the plunging depth, so the control makes a full retract after each infeed. Then it moves at FMAX back to 0 mm above the last depth (the advance stop distance is 0). The chain makes only small chip-break hops and feeds down.
- DEEP posts `G200` with `Q202` = the peck and `Q200=+0`. After each infeed, cycle 200 retracts and then moves at FMAX to the set-up clearance above the last depth. With Q200=0, that is the last depth itself. The chain rapids up to R and then feeds down from R.
- In both cases the tool moves at FMAX to the cut face in the hole. The simulation and the gouge check read the chain, so they do not see these moves. The comment at `heidenhain.cps:858-859` says the post wants "a conservative feed re-approach". The words do the opposite.

Expected: the native cycle does the motion of the checked chain, or the post writes the explicit chain.
- After a full retract, the tool goes back at FMAX only to a positive advance distance above the last depth. It feeds the remaining distance.
- PECK posts chip breaks inside the infeed, not a full retract after each peck.
- DEEP does not rapid to 0 mm above the last depth.

Evidence (upstream/main `1c0152c91`):
- `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:814`: PECK selects `G205`, DEEP selects `G200`.
- `heidenhain.cps:844-850`: a native peck only when the clearance is 0. Else the post writes the explicit chain.
- `heidenhain.cps:851-853`: `Q202` = the peck.
- `heidenhain.cps:866-867`: `Q258=0`, `Q259=0`, `Q257` = the peck, `Q205` = the peck.
- `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs:134-160`: PECK hops up by `CHIP_BREAK`; DEEP rapids to R and feeds down from R.
- Golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/heidenhain/drill_peck.nc`, block N100, shows the `G205` output.
- HEIDENHAIN TNC 640 cycle programming manual (ID 892905-25), cycles 200 and 205.

Found by the post audit against the HEIDENHAIN manuals (#4130).

Done means:
- `G205` and `G200` pecks keep a positive feed approach above the last depth, or the post writes the explicit chain for them.
- The posted PECK and DEEP motion agrees with the chain.
- A test pins the Q words of PECK and DEEP, and the goldens are updated.
